Ergane

Privacy policy

Last updated 20 October 2026

The short version

Ergane is a pottery journal. Your journal stays on your phone.

An account is optional. If you make one, the app sends our server your email address, your profile, only what you choose to share, when you tap to share it, and, if you turn on notifications, an address for your phone. Your journal never syncs to our server.

The app has no analytics, no tracking and no adverts.

When it opens, the app asks Expo for a new update and our server for the latest version number. These checks send nothing about you or your journal.

This policy covers the studio beta on TestFlight. We will update it before the public release.

Who we are

Ergane is run by an independent developer in the United Kingdom. In this policy, "we" and "us" mean the person who runs Ergane.

We decide how your data is used, so we are the controller under UK data protection law. You can reach us at hello@ergane.works.

What the app stores on your phone

The app stores what you enter:

  • Your builds: names, dates, notes, ratings, clays, techniques, tools, drying, firings and their fees, glaze layers, measurements, repairs, and what happened to each piece, with any sale price.
  • Your library: clays, glazes, glaze recipes, tools, techniques, firing presets and reference objects.
  • Your photos, and the pages you design for your builds.
  • Your settings, such as units, currency and saved colours.

All of it is kept in the app's own storage on your phone. We cannot see it, and we never receive a copy, unless you share a page from it.

If you make an account

Accounts are optional and for people aged 18 or over. The journal works without one.

An account holds:

  • Your email address. We send it a 6-digit code each time you sign in.
  • Your handle, which everyone signed in can see.
  • If you add them, a profile photo, a display name and a bio.
  • Whether your profile is public or private. Everyone signed in sees a private profile's handle and photo. A public profile also shows its display name and bio.

Before we make your profile, you tick that you are 18 or over and that you agree to the terms. We do not store the ticks: the profile exists only once you have ticked both.

The app keeps you signed in with a small file on your phone, apart from your journal. It never goes in an export.

We use this data to run your account and the sharing you ask for. Our lawful basis is that you asked us to provide that service.

What you choose to share

The app sends something to our server only when you tap to send it:

  • A page from a build, when you tap Share or Update shared copy: the words the page shows, its layout, and the photos you leave ticked. Hidden lines, unused photos, captions and file names stay on your phone. Prices and outcome notes go only if you tick them.
  • Who you follow, follow requests and approvals, followers you remove, and people you block.
  • Reports you make: what you reported, the reason and any details you type. Appeals you make: what you appeal and the words you type.
  • Clubs and groups you make, join, ask to join or leave, and your role in them. When you run a club or group, its name, handle, description, location or area, photo, rules and places, and whether a club is a studio or a community.
  • When you run a studio, its website or social page, and its Google Maps link, from which our server reads the studio's place on a map. Its owners can add a phone number and an email address for the studio.
  • Organisations you make or run: the name, the rules and the public or private setting shared with every club, which clubs are in it, and who owns it.
  • Club posts, discussion posts with up to 4 photos, and replies.
  • Comments you write on shared pages. On your own pages, whether comments are on, any comment you hide, and any poll you add: its question and options.
  • Your vote in a poll.
  • Events you make, and the dates you say you are going to.
  • When you run a club or group, items you add to its library or change there: the name and details you type or copy from your own library, such as what the maker says about a glaze's safety and its firing range, a glaze's recipe, a note, and up to 4 photos. Prices never go.
  • Glazes you share to a club: the glaze's name, details and notes, such as what the maker says about its safety and its firing range, and up to 4 test tile photos. Its recipe goes only if you tick Include recipe.
  • Pieces: a photo from one of your shared pages that you add to a library glaze, with any words you type. No new photo uploads.
  • Your ceramics journey, when you tap Share journey or Update journey: which of your shared pages are on it, their order, and which of their photos to show. Builds you have not shared stay on your phone. No new photo uploads.
  • Swap requests: which of your shared glazes you offer for another member's, and their answer. A request holds no words.

Photos go up as smaller copies made afresh on your phone, so they carry no location or camera details.

Who sees what you share:

  • A page for followers reaches your followers. A public page reaches everyone signed in, while your profile is public, and shows in the Everyone feed.
  • A page, post or event in a club or group reaches the people its audience lets in. A Public page in a public club reaches anyone signed in, even when your profile is private.
  • A club's or group's people see who belongs to it. People outside see that you belong to a public club only if you turn on Show my membership.
  • Anyone signed in sees whether a club is a studio or a community, and whether a studio is confirmed. Once it is confirmed, whoever can see the club sees its website. Only a studio's owners and our moderators see its phone number and email address.
  • Anyone signed in sees an organisation's name and its clubs. Only its owners see who owns it, and each club's number of members, drop-ins and requests, never names.
  • Who is going to an event shows by name to the club's or group's people. Everyone else sees a count.
  • A club's library shows to the club's people, and a group's to whoever can see the group. A library glaze's recipe shows to them only when Recipe public is on. When it is off, only the club's owners and admins, or the group's organisers, see it. A piece shows its photo to everyone who sees the library, even when its page is for your followers only. A glaze you share to a club reaches the audience you chose, with your handle.
  • A swap request shows only to you and the member you asked.
  • Your journey shows on your profile to people who can see your profile, and each sees only the pieces whose pages they can open. Their phone cuts out each piece from the page's photo itself.
  • A comment shows, with your handle, to everyone who can see the page, while its sharer has comments on. The sharer can hide it.
  • Nobody sees who voted for what in a poll, the person who asked included. People see the number of votes for each option.
  • The person you follow sees your follow or request. Someone you block is never told.
  • The person you report is never told who reported them.

People who are not signed in see nothing, apart from a club's name and photo on its join page, for a club whose join link is on.

A web address someone wrote, in a bio, club rules, a post, a reply, a comment or an event, and a confirmed studio's website, opens only if you tap it and then tap Open. Your phone's browser then visits that site, which sees your visit as it sees any visitor's. That site's own privacy policy covers it. The app sends nothing to it.

Anyone who saw something you shared could have taken a screenshot.

Checks during the beta

A word list on our server checks handles, display names, bios, club names and page titles. If one holds a word we do not allow, we refuse it and tell you why. We do not record what was refused.

If the words on a page, post, reply, comment, poll, event, library item, shared glaze or piece hold a slur, it waits for a moderator. Nobody else sees it until a moderator has looked. You see "Waiting for review".

During the beta, no outside moderation service checks what you share. Pages, photos and posts reach the people you chose straight away. Before the public release, an automated service will check them first, and we will update this policy to name it.

We check that a studio is real before it shows as one. If its email address is at its website's address, we email a code there, and the right code confirms it. Otherwise a moderator looks at its website, Maps link, phone number or email address, and confirms or declines it. Its owners and admins are told, and can appeal a decline once.

A moderator reads every report. A moderator can hide or remove what breaks the terms, and suspend an account. Each action and its reason go in a log. We tell you in the app what we did and why, and you can appeal once.

Our lawful basis for checks and moderation is our legitimate interests: keeping Ergane safe, and meeting our duties under the Online Safety Act.

Where your data is held

Supabase runs our server, in its London data centre. Supabase is a US company, so its staff may reach the data from outside the UK to run the service.

Brevo, a French company, emails your sign-in codes, and a studio's code, from its data centres in the European Union. It handles the email address and the code.

To find a studio's place on a map, our server opens its Google Maps link once, at Google. Google sees a request from our server, not from you.

Expo, a US company, delivers app updates, signed in or not. For each check it receives your IP address, your phone's type, the app's version and a random number the app makes for this phone. It never receives your journal or your account.

Expo also delivers notifications if you turn them on. It handles an address for your phone and the words of each notification, and passes them to Apple or Google.

These providers work for us under their data processing terms, which cover data that leaves the UK. We do not sell your data or share it for marketing.

How long we keep it

  • Your account and profile: until you delete your account.
  • A shared page and its photos: until you stop sharing it, delete the build, or delete your account.
  • Follows, blocks, memberships, posts and replies: until you remove them or delete your account.
  • Clubs, groups and events you make belong to the club. They stay with the club after you delete your account, without your name. So do items you add to a club's or group's library.
  • An organisation: until an owner deletes it, or until its last owner deletes their account and no owner of its clubs can take over.
  • Glazes you share to a club, pieces and swap requests: until you remove them, leave the club, or delete your account.
  • Comments, polls and votes: until you delete them, the page stops being shared, or you delete your account.
  • Your journey: until you update it, the page stops being shared, or you delete your account.
  • Going to an event: until 90 days after the date.
  • Your phone's notification address: until you sign out, delete your account, or the phone stops taking notifications.
  • Notifications: deleted from our server 7 days after we make them.
  • An upload that never finishes: deleted after 24 hours.
  • Reports, appeals and moderation records: while the beta runs. Before the public release, we will delete them or say here how long we keep them.
  • A studio's phone number and email address: until an owner changes them, the club becomes a community, or it is archived. A studio's code: until it is used, or replaced by a new one. Each lasts 15 minutes.
  • Sign-in and studio code emails: Brevo keeps a record of each one for 1 month.
  • Server logs: Supabase keeps technical logs, such as the internet address your phone connected from, for 1 day.

During the beta, our server keeps no backups. What you delete goes from our server at once.

Deleting your data

Your account:

  • Go to Settings, Account, Delete account. The app asks for a new sign-in code first.
  • It removes your account, profile, shared pages, photos, follows, blocks, club and group memberships, posts, replies, comments, polls, votes, the dates you are going to, glazes you shared to clubs, pieces, swap requests, your journey, your phone's notification address, your notifications and appeals from our server.
  • A club where you were the only owner passes to its admin who joined first, then its member who joined first. With neither, it is archived.
  • An organisation where you were the only owner passes to the owner of one of its clubs who joined that club first. With nobody, it ends, and its clubs keep their settings.
  • Reports you made stay, without your name, so a moderator can still act on them.
  • Your journal stays on your phone.
  • To delete your account without the app, email hello@ergane.works from the address you sign in with.

Your journal:

  • In the app, you can delete a build. That removes its records, its photos and its page from your phone, and the app's most recent export file and PDF. If the build is shared, it stops sharing it. You can also delete single photos, firings, glaze layers, measurements and repairs.
  • Archiving a library item, such as a clay or a glaze, hides it and keeps it on your phone.
  • To remove everything on your phone, delete the app. Delete your account first if you have one.
  • Export files you saved or sent elsewhere stay where you put them. Delete them there.
  • A phone backup may hold an older copy until the backup is replaced or deleted.

What the app does not do

  • No analytics or crash reporting. The app does not report how you use it.
  • No tracking and no advertising. The app has no advertising identifiers.
  • No syncing. Your journal never goes to our server. Keep an export as your backup.
  • No location. The app never asks for your location.
  • Nothing about you without an account. Signed out, the app only checks for a new version. See App updates.

On Android, the store may list standard permissions, such as network access, that the tools used to build the app declare. Ergane uses network access only for your account, what you share and app updates.

Camera and photo library

Your phone asks for permission the first time the app needs the camera. The app uses the camera only when you tap to take a photo of a build, a glaze test tile, a profile, a club or a post.

When you choose a photo from your library, the app receives only the photos you pick.

The app makes its own smaller copy of each photo and keeps it in its own storage. It reads the date the photo was taken. The app's copy does not keep the location or camera details from the original.

The app does not use the microphone.

You can switch off camera or photo access at any time in your phone's Settings. The rest of the app still works.

Calendar

When you are going to a club or group event, Add to calendar opens your phone's own New event screen, filled in with that one date. You choose whether to save it.

The app never reads your calendar, and nothing about your calendar leaves your phone.

On most phones this needs no permission. On an iPhone with iOS 16, your phone asks once for calendar access. You can switch it off at any time in your phone's Settings.

Notifications

With an account, the app can send you notifications:

  • Requests: when someone asks to follow you, or to join a club, group or event you run, and when a request of yours is accepted. A declined request sends nothing.
  • Events you are going to: a reminder at 6pm the day before, and a notice if the time or place changes or it is cancelled.

The app asks first, once, and your phone asks for permission only if you tap Turn on. Settings has a Requests switch and an Events switch. You can turn all notifications off in your phone's Settings.

When you allow notifications, the app gets an address for your phone from Expo and sends it to our server with your account. To send a notification, our server sends its words and that address to Expo, which passes them to Apple or Google to show on your phone.

Notifications name people, clubs, groups and events, such as "@ana asked to join Hackney Clay Club." They can show on your lock screen. Your phone's Settings can hide what they say there.

We use notifications only for these messages, never for marketing. Our lawful basis is that you asked us to provide that service.

App updates

Each time it opens, the app checks for a new version, signed in or not:

  • It asks Expo for a fix to the app. Expo sees your IP address, your phone's type, the app's version and a random number the app makes for this phone. A fix downloads in the background and takes effect the next time the app opens.
  • It asks our server for the latest version number. Our server sees your IP address and nothing else.

Neither check sends your journal, your account or anything you have typed. If a newer version is in the App Store or TestFlight, the app says so. Update opens the store. If your version no longer works with our server, your account, sharing and clubs wait until you update. Your journal still works.

Our lawful basis is our legitimate interests: keeping the app working and safe.

Export and import

Export data makes one zip file with your records and photos, then opens your phone's share sheet. You choose where the file goes, for example Files, Google Drive, Dropbox or an email.

Once you save or send an export file, it is outside the app. The service or person you send it to handles it under their own privacy policy. An export can include notes and photos, so share it with care.

You can also save or send a single photo from a build, with a long press, or a page or your whole journal as a PDF for printing, through the same share sheet. The app makes these on your phone and sends them nowhere itself. Its copy of a photo holds no location.

The app keeps the most recent PDF in its temporary storage until your next PDF, until you delete a build, or until your phone clears it.

The app keeps the most recent export file in its temporary storage until your next export, until you delete a build, or until your phone clears it.

Import data reads a zip file that you choose and adds its contents to the app. The file is read on your phone.

Phone backups

If you have switched on iCloud Backup or Google backup, your phone may include the app's data in that backup. Apple or Google runs that service, and you control it in your phone's Settings. We have no access to those backups.

If you email us

If you write to hello@ergane.works or support@ergane.works, we receive your email address and whatever you put in your message.

Send feedback, in the app's Settings, opens your own mail app with a draft to support@ergane.works. The draft names the app version, your phone's model and its system version, to help us fix problems. You can read or delete those lines before you send. The app sends nothing itself, and nothing from your journal goes in the draft.

We use your message only to read and answer it. Our lawful basis is legitimate interests: replying to people who contact us.

Our domain and email providers handle the message for us so that it reaches our inbox. We do not sell it, share it for marketing or add you to a mailing list.

We keep your message only for as long as we need it to deal with your request.

Your rights

You have the right to ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to get it in a form you can move elsewhere, and to object to or restrict how we use it. Email us and we will reply within one month.

If you are unhappy with how we have handled your data, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office, the UK regulator, at ico.org.uk.

The website

The website at ergane.works uses no cookies, no analytics and no tracking.

GitHub hosts the website. Like any web host, GitHub receives the IP address of each visitor and keeps logs for security. GitHub's own privacy statement covers that.

A club's join page, at ergane.works/join and the club's handle, asks our server for that club's name and photo, and nothing else. Our server sees the visitor's IP address, which Supabase keeps in its technical logs for 1 day. The page sets no cookie and stores nothing. If you have Ergane on your phone, the link opens the club in the app instead.

Children

Accounts are for people aged 18 or over. If we learn that someone under 18 has an account, we delete it.

The journal on its own collects no personal data from anyone, of any age.

Changes to this policy

If Ergane changes in a way that affects your privacy, we will update this policy before the change reaches you. The date at the top shows when it last changed. The latest version is always at ergane.works/privacy and in the app under Settings.

Contact

Questions about this policy or your privacy: hello@ergane.works.
